canonicalFacts.claim: COPD is characterized by progressive airflow obstruction confirmed by post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio less than 0.70
Tobacco smoking is the leading cause of COPD but other environmental factors including indoor air pollutants contribute to risk
COPD exacerbations are associated with worse quality of life, increased hospitalizations, and increased mortality
Inhaler therapy is the backbone of COPD treatment and should be complemented by smoking cessation, pulmonary rehabilitation, and treatment of comorbidities
Up to 78% of COPD exacerbations are due to bacterial infections, viral infections, or both

redFlags: Long-term oxygen therapy indicated only in hypoxemic patients
Target oxygen saturations 88-92% in COPD exacerbations unless CO2 levels normal

excludedAgents.name: N-acetylcysteine
excludedAgents.reason: High-dose N-acetylcysteine (600mg twice daily) failed to reduce exacerbations or improve lung function in mild-to-moderate COPD patients in a 2-year randomized controlled trial

excludedAgents.name: Statins
excludedAgents.reason: Cochrane review found statins showed no significant benefit versus placebo for COPD exacerbations or clinical outcomes

excludedAgents.name: Carbocysteine
excludedAgents.reason: Carbocysteine (500mg thrice daily) showed no significant benefit for exacerbation rate or pulmonary function in mild-to-moderate COPD patients in a 12-month randomized controlled trial

excludedAgents.name: Tadalafil
excludedAgents.reason: Tadalafil (40mg daily) failed to improve the primary endpoint of 6-minute walk distance in veterans with COPD-pulmonary hypertension in a 12-month randomized trial
